MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 9, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:02 p.m., on April 9, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 4, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case); and threat to
  Public Services or Facilities; Consultation with City Attorney and Related Experts.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with four Council Members present (Council Member Bucknum was
absent).

City Council Minutes  1  April 9, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received an update and gave direction
to staff but no reportable action occurred in Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Dylan Bruette-Riordan

NATIONAL ANTHEM: Capistrano Valley High School Saxophone Quartet

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize the Spring AYSO Region 84 Girls U10 Team "Impact" as the Western State
  Champions

  Mayor Raths presented certificates of recognition to the coaches and members of AYSO
  soccer team Impact.

P2. Featured Businesses of the Month

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Adrien Diaz of Mary Kay Cosmetics.

P3. Road to the 2020 Census

  Partnership Specialist Bao Nguyen of the U.S. Census Bureau presented an overview of the
  2020 census program.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ryan Farsai, Mission Viejo: announced that he is now the proud owner of property in Oregon and
he will be reorganizing his California yoga corporation to an Oregon corporation.

Pauline Finorio, M.V.: requested that a gate be installed at the entrance to the Las Flores
condominium complex at the corner of La Crescenta and Las Flores. She also asked for speed
bumps on City streets outside the complex and for a status on sidewalk repairs in front of her unit.

Michael Leonard and John Salamy, Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce Board Members:
thanked City staff for hosting the Chamber of Commerce monthly mixer at city hall last week.
Michael said it was great to learn about the different departments and how the City supports the
businesses and members of the community.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  2  April 9, 2019
 AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of March 26, 2019, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated March 15, 2019 in the Amount of $2,809,639.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated March 22, 2019 in the Amount of $318,479.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2019

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for February 2019

  Received and filed.

6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for February 2019

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2019

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

8.  Fiscal Year 2019/20 Senate Bill 1 Road Repair and Accountability Act

  Council Member Sachs asked staff to consider repairing the stretch of road on Olympiad
  between Alicia Parkway and the fire station.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon responded that staff has just received bids for that
  project and it will come before the City Council for award of a contract very soon.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  adopt Resolution 19-05 Adopting a List of Projects for Fiscal Year 2019/20 Funded by
  Senate Bill 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017.

City Council Minutes  3  April 9, 2019
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

OLD BUSINESS

9.  Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract 2019-2021

  Community Services Manager Lydie Gutfeld presented the staff report.

  Saddleback Valley Unified School District representatives Kurt Walker, District
  Supervisor, Elizabeth Figarsky, Supervisor, and Stephanie Goodwin, Assistant Coordinator,
  presented and overview of the Kid’s Factory after school and summer programs.

  Council Member Kelley asked the Saddleback Unified School District staff to consider the
  possibility of a family discount. She also requested that the Kids Factory flier be updated to
  note that the program is subsidized by the City of Mission Viejo.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to approve
  the Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract for 2019-2021 and
  increase participant fee by $15 per school year and $10 per summer session as recommended
  by the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

10. Capital Improvement Program Prioritization as Recommended by the Community
  Services Commission

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Chris Welch, M.V.: requested that consideration be given to parking, snack bar and restroom
  issues at Craycraft Park.

  The following requested ballfield lights and new restrooms at the Youth Athletic Park:
  Garrett Mitton, President of South Mission Viejo Little League; Jeff Corrao, Chief Umpire
  of North Mission Viejo Little League; and Michael Boyd, M.V.

  Kraig Erickson, M.V.: asked the Council to consider the addition of play equipment at La
  Mancha Park.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

City Council Minutes  4  April 9, 2019
 11. FY 2019-21 Revenue Projections

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas outlined the 2019-21 revenue projections
  and answered the City Council Members' questions.

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

13. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

14. Analysis of Contract Law Enforcement Services Costs and Methodology for Contract
  Cities Report

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum was absent.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Orange County Taxpayers Association
Assembly Delegation meeting where she heard a very informative presentation on the Proposition
13 split roll moderated by Carolyn Cavecche. She said that attendees came away with a lot to think
about and worry about. Council Member Kelley announced that the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee will be hosting its annual Boots Beer & BBQ event to support the City’s adopted Marines
on Sunday, July 21, 2019, from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m. Tickets are $25 per person and they will be
available for in-person purchase at the Norman P. Murray Community Center or online at
mvcommunityfoundation.org. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character
word for the month of April is service and she shared a quote from Mother Teresa: “Never worry
about numbers. Help one person at a time and always start with the person nearest you.”

City Council Minutes  5  April 9, 2019
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs discussed his attendance at a League of California Cities presentation from
Michael Coleman on the major budget proposals affecting cities. He said the state legislature is
looking at new taxes for things like tires, tax services, lawn care, etcetera. Council Member Sachs
noted that he recently saw two national news stations reporting on the taxes that California is taking
on and he said the state is dangerously close to splitting Proposition 13 for business properties,
with residential properties coming next. Council Member Sachs outlined his attendance at Senator
Bates and Assemblyman Brough's South Orange County Senior Day last week. He said there was
a full house and there were many good resources for seniors, including a presentation by District
Attorney Todd Spitzer on senior scams.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he too attended the South Orange County Economic
Coalition presentation on the Proposition 13 split roll where he learned that the county would have
to assess commercial properties differently than it does residential properties. He stated that the
taxes will go sky high for commercial buildings and most of the businesses that serve the City pay
the property tax on the buildings that they lease. The Proposition 13 split would equate to higher
prices for goods and services so businesses can afford to pay the taxes. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
discussed his attendance at the VIP mixer at the Marguerite Tennis Center in support of the Konrad
Reuland Foundation. Konrad was a former Mission Viejo High School football player who went
on to play professional ball and later died of a brain aneurism. After his death, Konrad’s organs
were donated to many recipients including Rod Carew who received his heart and a kidney. The
Reuland family attended the event and Mayor Pro Tem Goodell said it was nice to be able to honor
one of Mission Viejo’s hometown heroes who gave everything. He concluded by reminding
residents that the FINA Diving Grand Prix will start on April 11 at the Marguerite Aquatics Center.
Mayor Pro Tem Goodell congratulated City staff on a beautiful job setting up for the event and he
encouraged residents to stop by and see some of the greatest divers in the world.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths announced that he attended the swearing in ceremony for the newly elected Orange
County Supervisor Don Wagner. He also attended Senior Day sponsored by Senator Bates and
Assemblyman Brough and he said the discussion of senior scams was very valuable. Mayor Raths
stated that he enjoyed his ride-along with Orange County Fire Authority Chief Capobianco during
which they visited all of the fire stations in town and the headquarters in Ladera Ranch. He outlined
his attendance at additional events including the VFW 6024 member meeting, a Rose Society of
Saddleback Mountain gathering, Marine Corps Day at Lake Mission Viejo and the City’s volunteer
recognition event where volunteers were honored for saving the City more than $600,000. In
closing, Mayor Raths noted that Assemblyman Brough has introduced a bill that would exempt
veterans from California income tax.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:42 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, April 23, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  6  April 9, 2019
 ______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 23, 2019

City Council Minutes  7  April 9, 2019
